speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia. To narrow this down, can you tell me if you have a known history of vitamin E deficiency or an issue with your small intestine absorption?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; the "drunken" gait is a classic sign of cerebellar or proprioceptive dysfunction. Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your extremities, and do you have a history of cystic fibrosis or chronic diarrhea which might suggest fat malabsorption?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Serum Vitamin E level and Full Blood Count. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain and Spinal Cord.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The normal Vitamin E levels and the specific MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement confirm PML rather than a deficiency-related ataxia. I need to immediately discontinue natalizumab and consider starting immunoglobulin therapy.
